digest.top_line: RTOG 3506 (STEEL): enzalutamide added to SRT + 24mo ADT in high-risk post-RP BCR, PFS HR 0.62 (80% CI 0.42-0.91, one-sided p=0.052); 2y BF 11% vs 19%.
digest.tldr: Prostate RT carried the day. STEEL is a randomized phase II screening signal for adding an ARSI to salvage RT + 24mo ADT in high-risk post-RP BCR. SRT dose and volume were not reported. REVELUTION's post hoc PROs favor relugolix over leuprolide with RT at 12 mo (IPSS 5.66 vs 9.22).

sites.intro: Both readouts change the hormonal partner given with RT, not the RT itself: an ARSI added to salvage RT + ADT, and oral vs injectable ADT alongside definitive RT.

studies.name: REVELUTION (relugolix vs leuprolide + RT, PROs)
studies.tldr: At 12 mo, relugolix vs leuprolide with RT: IPSS 5.66 vs 9.22 (p=0.039), EPIC-CP total 12.25 vs 17.25 (p=0.02); post hoc.
details: 🔍 RCT 1:1, N=65, localized intermediate- or high-risk PCa, RT + ADT, no prior ADT
🔍 Parent trial 1° EP: 12-mo change in total coronary plaque volume by coronary CT angiography
⚠️ This QoL analysis is post hoc; PROs were not the parent trial's endpoint
💊 Relugolix oral daily vs leuprolide injection every 3 months, both with RT
📊 Two further EPIC-CP domains (bowel, vitality) read 0.4 vs 2.1 (P=.003) and 1.8 vs 3.2 (P=.053) per slide OCR
📊 No 12-mo difference in EPIC-CP incontinence, irritation, sexual, or SHIM (all P≥.15)
⚠️ Mean T at 12 mo higher on relugolix (199.7 vs 142.0 ng/dL); ADT on/off status at 12 mo not stated in source
⚠️ Small N, single parent trial, unblinded route difference (oral vs injection) could shape PRO reporting
🔗 Context: HERO established relugolix vs leuprolide in advanced PCa; REVELUTION adds PRO data in the RT setting

figures.caption: Covariate-adjusted PROs. 12 months: IPSS 5.7 vs 9.2; EPIC-CP total 12.3 vs 17.3 (P = .020); 0.4 vs 2.1 (P=.003); 1.8 vs 3.2 (P = .053).

verdict.rationale: Post hoc QoL analysis of a trial powered for coronary plaque, N=65; PRO differences not a prespecified endpoint and route of administration unblinded.
verdict.audience: Localized intermediate/high-risk prostate cancer, RT + ADT, ADT-naive

studies.significance: The PRO gap tracks with faster testosterone recovery on relugolix (mean 199.7 vs 142.0 ng/dL at 12 mo, P=.010), which plausibly explains better urinary and EPIC-CP total scores. For RT + short-course ADT, that recovery kinetic is the relevant variable when choosing GnRH agent; whether it costs anything in biochemical control is untested here.
studies.monday_clinic: In an ADT-naive man with localized intermediate- or high-risk prostate cancer starting RT + ADT, this offers hypothesis-level support for relugolix on 12-mo urinary and overall PRO burden; it says nothing about biochemical or oncologic control.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Post hoc QoL analysis** of a 1:1 randomized trial, **N=65**. Parent trial **primary:** 12-month change in total coronary plaque volume by coronary CT angiography.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Localized intermediate- or high-risk prostate cancer**, receiving RT + ADT, **no prior ADT**.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **Relugolix** oral daily vs **leuprolide** injection every 3 months, each with RT.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Relugolix favored on IPSS and EPIC-CP total at 12 mo; incontinence, irritation, sexual and SHIM did **not differ** (all P≥.15). Mean testosterone at 12 mo **199.7 vs 142.0 ng/dL** (P=.010), higher on relugolix.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: HERO compared relugolix with leuprolide in advanced prostate cancer; this analysis extends the comparison to the curative RT setting, but only on PROs and testosterone, not disease control.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents ADT-naive localized intermediate- or high-risk prostate cancer treated with RT + ADT. Does not represent metastatic, castration-resistant, or post-prostatectomy salvage settings.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Open route difference (oral vs injection) could bias self-reported outcomes. Whether pts were still on ADT at 12 mo is not stated, so the testosterone and PRO gaps may reflect recovery timing rather than on-treatment tolerability.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The urinary and global PRO advantage aligns with faster testosterone recovery on relugolix. Whether that recovery trades against biochemical control after RT is the unanswered question.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: In RT + ADT for localized intermediate/high-risk disease, relugolix was linked to lower IPSS (5.66 vs 9.22) and EPIC-CP total (12.25 vs 17.25) at 12 mo, with higher mean testosterone. That informs agent choice when RT-related urinary and bowel symptoms are the concern, pending oncologic data.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Mean testosterone at 12 mo was higher on relugolix (199.7 vs 142.0 ng/dL), consistent with faster recovery after an oral antagonist. The PRO benefit may reflect that recovery; disease control with relugolix in this curative RT setting is not addressed by this analysis.

open_questions: Does faster testosterone recovery on relugolix affect biochemical control after RT?
Do PRO differences hold in a prespecified, larger trial?

related_trials.brief_title: RecoverPC: Relugolix vs GnRH Agonist in Quality of Life
related_trials.brief_summary:
This study is testing the way that approved androgen deprivation therapy treatments, Leuprolide and Relugolix, for prostate cancer affect quality of life, blood levels, cholesterol, and blood sugar. The drugs are already standard treatment for people with prostate cancer, and the drugs will be used as described in their label.

The names of the study drugs involved in this study are:

* Leuprolide (type of ADT)
* Relugolix (type of ADT)

studies.name: RTOG 3506 (STEEL)
studies.tldr: PFS HR 0.62 (80% CI 0.42-0.91, one-sided p=0.052) adding enzalutamide to SRT + 24mo ADT in high-risk post-RP BCR; BF at 2y 11% vs 19%.
details: 🔍 Randomized phase II, 1:1, n=188, mFU 33.1 mos
🔍 Primary endpoint PFS, designed with one-sided type I error=0.10 (screening design)
💊 Control: SRT + 24 months GnRHa · Exp: SRT + 24 months GnRHa + enzalutamide 160 mg

details.text: 🔍 Eligibility: BCR after RP with PSA ≥0.2 ng/mL (or ≥0.1 ng/mL ultrasensitive) + ≥1 aggressive feature

details: 📊 Biochemical failure at 2 yrs: 11% vs 19% (enza + ADT vs ADT)

details.text: 📊 Gr 3-4 AEs higher with enza in the top two rows

details: ⚠️ SRT dose, fractionation and target volume (bed vs pelvic nodes) not reported in source
🔗 Builds on the SRT + ADT evidence base (RTOG 9601, GETUG-AFU 16, SPPORT); tests ARSI intensification on a 24mo backbone

figures.caption: Randomize 1:1: SRT + 24 months GnRHa ± enzalutamide 160 mg. Primary endpoint PFS (one-sided type I error=0.10).

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase II screening design: one-sided α 0.10, 80% CI, surrogate PFS endpoint, 33mo median f/u. Needs phase III confirmation before ARSI intensification with SRT.
verdict.audience: Post-RP BCR with ≥1 high-risk feature, receiving SRT + 24mo ADT

studies.significance: Both arms received SRT + 24 months GnRHa, so the trial isolates ARSI intensification, not the RT contribution; SRT dose and field are not reported in source. BF at 2y dropped 19% to 11%, but Gr 3-4 lymphopenia rose 15% vs 5%, worth weighing if pelvic nodal fields are in the plan.
studies.monday_clinic: In post-RP BCR with Gleason 8-10, SVI, pN1, persistent PSA or PSA ≥0.7 already planned for SRT + 24 months ADT, this supports discussing enzalutamide as investigational intensification; it does not extend to lower-risk BCR or shorter ADT courses.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Randomized phase II**, 1:1, **n=188**, final results. Median follow-up **33.1 mos**. Designed with a **one-sided type I error of 0.10**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **BCR after RP** with PSA ≥0.2 ng/mL (or ≥0.1 ng/mL ultrasensitive) plus **≥1 aggressive feature**: Gleason 8-10, SVI, pN1, persistently elevated post-RP PSA >0.1 ng/mL, or PSA ≥0.7 ng/mL.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Control: **24 months GnRHa**. Experimental: 24 months GnRHa + **enzalutamide 160 mg**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **Salvage RT in both arms.** Dose, fractionation and target volume (prostate bed vs pelvic nodes) are **not reported in source**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** PFS. **Secondary:** biochemical failure, hormone-refractory disease, distant metastasis, cause-specific and overall mortality, physician- and patient-reported toxicity, fatigue (PROMIS-F SF 7a), global QoL (EQ-5D-5L).

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: More **Gr 3-4 lymphopenia** with enza, 13 (15%) vs 5 (5%), and Gr 3-4 hypertension 7 (8%) vs 5 (5%). All-grade hot flashes 81% vs 70%.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: RTOG 9601, GETUG-AFU 16 and SPPORT established adding ADT to SRT; STEEL asks the next question, whether an **ARSI on top of long-course ADT** adds further. EMBARK tested enzalutamide in high-risk BCR without RT, a different setting.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents post-RP BCR with high-risk pathology or PSA kinetics receiving SRT + 24 months ADT. Does not represent lower-risk BCR, short-course ADT, or RT-naive intact-prostate disease.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: SRT technique not reported, so RT transferability can't be judged. PFS definition and blinding not stated in source. The 24-month ADT control is itself intensified relative to many current practices.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The signal clears the trial's own screening threshold, but **no OS or metastasis data** in source, so the cost in lymphopenia and hypertension is set against a surrogate benefit only. The question is now phase III-ready, not practice-ready.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: RT was fixed across arms, so this informs what to pair with SRT, not dose or field; technique is not reported in source. BF at 2y 11% vs 19% suggests the SRT + 24mo ADT backbone still leaves room for intensification in high-risk BCR.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Enzalutamide 160 mg on top of 24 months GnRHa cut PFS hazard (HR 0.62, 80% CI 0.42-0.91) in a screening design. Gr 3-4 lymphopenia 15% vs 5% and hypertension 8% vs 5% are the toxicity trade to weigh pending phase III.

open_questions: Does PFS gain translate to MFS or OS?
Phase III confirmation of ARSI intensification with salvage RT
Role of pelvic nodal RT alongside enhanced AR suppression
